result:
Before I write it up, one quick decision that's yours: how it gets built. We've settled what it does; this is just where it lives.

**1. Add it to the existing taproom app (my recommendation).** New tables for batches, sacks, and bottling runs go in the same SQLite database, with new pages in the same Flask app on the office Pi. It's one thing to run, back up, and keep updated, and it follows patterns the code already uses. The cost is that the taproom tabs and brewing records share one app, so a bad update to one could take both down until it's fixed.

**2. Build a separate small app on the same Pi.** Batch tracking gets its own Flask app and its own database. Brewing and the taproom can't break each other, and either can be changed alone. The cost is two apps to start, back up, and keep running on one small machine, with some code duplicated between them.

I ruled out off-the-shelf brewery software. It would mean a subscription, your records living off-site, and working around the label printer and scanning setup we just designed.

I recommend option 1. It's one Pi with one office, and the tabs app is small enough that adding to it stays manageable.

This is a project-sized piece of work, so I'll write it as a full design document. A reviewer will read it before you see it, and I may come back once with a few questions only you can answer. The folder isn't under version control yet, so I'll set that up to save the document, unless you'd rather I didn't.

Which way do you want to go, or should I just take option 1?
